subject: optometry
intro: Optometry study leads to the eye-care professions — the clinicians who examine and treat vision, the surgeons who operate on the eye, and the makers and managers behind every pair of glasses.

roles.title: Optometrists
roles.what: Diagnose, manage and treat conditions of the human eye and visual system — examining eyes, diagnosing impairments, prescribing corrective lenses, and in many states prescribing therapeutic drugs for specific eye conditions.
roles.where: Units 2 and 3 — ocular anatomy, subjective refraction, accommodation and convergence — are the core clinical exam; unit 4's spectacle and contact lens optics and low vision aids are the prescribing toolkit; units 5 and 6 supply the disease knowledge.

roles.title: Ophthalmologists, Except Pediatric
roles.what: Diagnose and perform surgery to treat and help prevent disorders and diseases of the eye, and provide vision services including glasses and contact lenses — the medical and surgical end of eye care.
roles.where: Unit 5's glaucoma, cataract and macular degeneration and unit 6's systemic disease and neuro-ophthalmic signs are the conditions ophthalmologists treat and operate on; unit 1's optics underpins the corrections they prescribe.

roles.title: Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
roles.what: Cut, grind and polish eyeglasses, contact lenses and other precision optical elements, then assemble and mount lenses into frames — turning a prescription into a finished optical product.
roles.where: Unit 1's refraction, vergence and prism theory and unit 4's spectacle and contact lens optics explain exactly what the technician must translate into surfaced, edged and mounted lenses.

roles.title: Medical and Health Services Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate health services — running clinics and departments, managing staff, budgets and compliance, and shaping how care is delivered in practices and hospitals.
roles.where: Unit 7 is the direct match — practice management, vision screening and epidemiology, ethics and law — covering the business, regulatory and public-health sides of running an optometry practice or eye-care department.
